findings.title: Remove NULs from shell-bound values before applying `@sh`
findings.body: On jq 1.6, I verified that `@sh` produces identical shell text for a NUL and the literal characters `\0`. Main’s `jq -r` followed by Bash command substitution drops the NUL. A session ID containing only a NUL therefore selects no merge grant on main, but the proposed decoder can select a nonempty grant filename. Normalize shell-bound values before quoting and continue deriving the agent key from the original JSON.

findings.title: Restrict each shell assignment to one scalar value
findings.body: `@sh` on a JSON array emits several shell words. If a caller supplies an array-valued `session_id`, evaluating the resulting assignment can execute its second element as a command under the hook’s account. An object instead makes `@sh` error, which can discard an otherwise valid guard decision. Main reads these values as data. The plan needs a type rule for each field before any generated assignment is evaluated.

findings.title: Give every optional field an explicit default in the combined record
findings.body: A normal `Edit` has no `tool_input.command`, and a normal `Bash` call has no edit path. Main’s separate `// empty` filters work because each missing value affects only its own assignment. I verified that interpolating one such filter into a combined jq string suppresses the entire record. That can lose the tool name and skip a strict edit denial. Preserve the per-field defaults, including the engine’s `nosession` fallback.

findings.title: Preserve trailing newlines in normalized edit-isolation paths
findings.body: Main reads each normalized path with `read -r -d ''`, which preserves a trailing newline. Applying the proposed newline stripping to those paths can change the isolation verdict. For example, a protected checkout can contain a regular file whose name ends in a newline and a sibling symlink with the trimmed name pointing outside. The current guard checks the regular file, while the trimmed path sends it to the symlink’s destination.

findings.title: Emit the malformed-patch flag even when there are no targets
findings.body: `host-input.py paths` can return `malformed_patch: true` with an empty `paths` array. Main tests the flag before it iterates the array. The plan leaves the record layout unspecified. If the combined jq read emits one record per `.paths[]`, it emits nothing for this case and the edit guard can silently allow a malformed patch. The flag must be available independently of the target count.

findings.title: Add the required contract for the benchmark directory
findings.body: This file makes `specs/pretool-dispatch/evidence/bench` a Python source directory, and the directory contains no `AGENTS.md`. The coverage gate enumerates tracked `.py` files, includes `specs/`, and requires a contract in the directory itself. The required `make test` lane will fail on this change.

findings.title: Reject failed or degraded hook runs before recording their latency
findings.body: `run()` discards the exit code and both output streams. A missing candidate script, a shell syntax error, or a fast dependency-degradation response can therefore look like a speedup. A stuck hook can also hang the benchmark indefinitely because there is no deadline. Validate the expected outcome for each fixture and bound each invocation before accepting its timing.

findings.title: Compare differential output at equivalent filesystem paths
findings.body: A strict owner-dispatch denial embeds the engine’s absolute `$SELF` path, the project root, and the waiver path in stdout. Running identical scripts from separate baseline and candidate trees already produces different messages. Use the same visible paths for both runs or normalize only the known fixture prefixes before comparing output, so the oracle can still catch a changed denial reason.

findings.title: Exercise merge-grant consumption in the differential
findings.body: The planned file comparison covers owner activity markers. It misses the merge guard’s session-scoped grant. If two sessions each have a one-shot grant and a decoding error selects the other session, the first call can return exactly the expected success message while consuming the wrong grant. Compare both grant files and the subsequent calls for both sessions.

findings.title: Make the Stop comparison observe a real gated edit
findings.body: PreToolUse records the baseline before the file changes. If the differential immediately invokes Stop, main normally allows because the working tree still matches that baseline. A candidate that loses actor attribution can return the same verdict. Apply the same gated edit in both fixtures before Stop and assert that the relevant baseline actor actually receives the expected block.

findings.title: Check stderr for payload disclosure on the new edge cases
findings.body: The edit-isolation suite requires empty stderr because inputs can include file contents. A decoder that prints a jq or shell diagnostic for an unexpected field type can expose input while preserving stdout, exit status, and state. The proposed differential would pass that regression. Include a synthetic marker in the malformed field and check stderr for the affected hook.

findings.title: Register the differential in the repository test lane
findings.body: `origin/main`’s Makefile invokes each hook test by name. Adding `hooks/test_hook_field_reads.py` alone leaves it outside both `make test` and CI’s `repository-gates` job. A later parser regression can therefore pass the required lanes even if the new differential would catch it.

findings.title: Measure serial-host and multi-target latency before accepting the change
findings.body: The acceptance rule checks only two parallel shell timings. OpenCode performs synchronous Git checks and runs the edit hooks for each patch target. Antigravity also processes targets through its bridge. A regression whose cost grows with the number of paths can slow either host while the single-file parallel `Edit` and `Bash` samples both pass.

findings.title: Resolve benchmark arguments before changing the child working directory
findings.body: The documented invocation accepts relative paths. With relative plugin roots and a separate project directory, Bash looks for each hook relative to the project instead of the directory where the harness was launched. A relative project path is also embedded in the edit payload and can be resolved twice. Canonicalize all three paths at startup.

findings.title: Make the pinned oracle available in shallow checkouts
findings.body: A depth-one checkout of the implementation commit need not contain `788470c`. The new test would fail during baseline extraction before exercising either parser, or lose its comparison if missing history is treated as a skip. Provide a pinned fixture or an explicit setup step that makes the baseline object available.

findings.title: Run the npm checks from the package directory
findings.body: The repository root has no `package.json`. Following the listed commands from the same directory as `make test` makes the standalone `npm test` and `npm run smoke:host` fail before running their checks. `make npm-publish-dry` already runs the package tests, and `make npm-host-smoke` invokes the smoke script from the correct directory.
